targets.authors: Robertson, Claire E., Nicolas Pröllochs, Kaoru Schwarzenegger, Philip Pärnamets, Jay J. Van Bavel, and Stefan Feuerriegel.
targets.title: Negativity Drives Online News Consumption.
targets.evidence_quote: As part of this broader initiative, we examine the reproducibility and robustness of the two central claims from Robertson et al. (2023), who investigate the impact of negative language on online news consumption.
targets.outcome_computational_quote: We successfully computationally reproduced the two central claims with identical numerical results using their codes as well as their analysis data and raw data with minimal effort.
targets.outcome_robustness_quote: Taken together, we find the effect of positivity is neither robust within semantic nor across lexical and semantic sentiment analysis paradigms.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Original-data/code analyses recover identical central estimates. Alternative semantic sentiment measures preserve the negativity claim but undermine the explicitly central positivity claim, so the aggregate robustness axis has challenges. Secondary reporting discrepancies do not negate recovery of the central estimates.
